title: Coronary territories and STEMI localisation
claims: The left main coronary artery divides into the LAD (anterior interventricular groove) and the circumflex (left AV groove).
The LAD supplies the anterior LV wall, the apex and the anterior 2/3 of the interventricular septum (septal perforators); diagonal branches supply the anterolateral wall.
The circumflex supplies the lateral LV wall through its obtuse marginal branches.
The RCA runs in the right AV groove and supplies the RV free wall (acute marginal branch), the SA node in about 60% and the AV node in about 80-90%.
Coronary dominance is defined by which artery gives the posterior descending artery (PDA); about 70-80% of people are right-dominant.
The PDA supplies the inferior LV wall and the posterior 1/3 of the septum.
The LAD is the most commonly occluded coronary artery.
Anterior (anteroseptal) STEMI from LAD occlusion: ST elevation in V1-V4.
Lateral STEMI from circumflex occlusion: ST elevation in I, aVL, V5-V6.
Posterior MI (often circumflex or RCA) shows ST depression with tall R waves in V1-V3; confirm with posterior leads V7-V9.
Inferior STEMI from RCA occlusion: ST elevation in II, III and aVF, with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL.
In inferior STEMI, ST elevation greater in III than in II favours the RCA over the circumflex.
Proximal RCA occlusion can cause RV infarction: ST elevation in V4R, hypotension, raised JVP and clear lungs.
RV infarction is preload dependent: give IV fluids and avoid nitrates.
Inferior MI often causes bradycardia and AV block at the AV node (AV nodal artery from the RCA); it is usually transient and treated with atropine, pacing if unstable.
The posteromedial papillary muscle has a single blood supply (PDA), so it is the one that ruptures after an inferior MI, causing acute mitral regurgitation.
The anterolateral papillary muscle has a dual supply (LAD and circumflex) and rarely ruptures.
STEMI reperfusion: primary PCI within 90 minutes of first medical contact, or fibrinolysis when PCI cannot be done within 120 minutes.
